findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data object will throw at runtime
findings.body: The new call `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object. Prisma's `updateMany` rejects an empty `data` argument with a validation error ("Argument `data` must provide at least one field"). Since the comment says the intent is to bump `updatedAt`, this call will throw every time `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` completes (i.e. on every calendar watch/unwatch cycle), breaking webhook-driven cache refresh. It should pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` instead.

findings.title: Cache status timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale, ignoring user locale
findings.body: The component formats `cacheUpdatedAt` with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, ignoring the user's selected locale even though the component already has `useLocale()`. All non-English users will see US-formatted dates. Should use the locale from `useLocale()`.

findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars, leaving stale cache status
findings.body: On successful cache deletion, the component only calls the optional `onSuccess` callback (which is only passed as `onChanged` in some usages). It never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike the disconnect mutation. If `onChanged` is undefined or does not refetch, the UI continues to show the old "Cache Status / Last updated" entry and the "Delete cached data" option even though the cache is gone, until a manual page refresh.

findings.title: Cache status lookup misses caches stored for in-memory delegation credentials
findings.body: For in-memory delegation credentials (negative credentialId), `CalendarCache` rows are keyed by `userId` + key rather than the (nonexistent) DB credentialId (see `CalendarCacheRepository.getCachedAvailability`). `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` only groups by `credentialId`, so delegated Google Calendar users will never see their cache status and cannot clear it from the UI, even though a cache exists and is actively served. Either look up by userId for delegation credentials or document the limitation.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds reports expired cache entries as active
findings.body: The groupBy query does not filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }`. A credential whose only cache rows have expired will still return an `updatedAt` value, so the UI will show a "Cache Status / Last updated" timestamp and a "Delete cached data" action for cache data that is no longer served. This is misleading and lets users trigger a no-op delete with a confirmation dialog.

findings.title: sed -i '' is macOS-only and fails on Linux
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` uses the BSD/macOS form of in-place editing; on GNU/Linux (Linux CI/dev containers) `sed -i ''` fails with "can't read : No such file or directory". Use a portable form (e.g. `sed -i.bak` + remove the backup) or detect the platform.

findings.title: dev:cron uses npx tsx but tsx is not a declared dependency
findings.body: The script was changed from `ts-node` to `npx tsx`, but `tsx` is not in dependencies or devDependencies (only `ts-node` is, and it remains unused for this script). `npx` will download `tsx` ad hoc on each run (or fail offline / behind a proxy). Add `tsx` to devDependencies.
